data.title: The Graph to Activate REO Step 5 on December 8th
data.description:
The Graph will activate REO Step 5 on December 8th. Indexers with more than 30 million GRT in total stake will need to serve qualifying queries on one subgraph per 3 million GRT, up from one per 4 million GRT; all other indexers will retain the 10-subgraph minimum.

Refer to the official tweet by GRT:

The Graph
@graphprotocol

REO Step 5 starts December 8

Indexers above 30M GRT total stake will need to serve qualifying queries on 1 Subgraph per 3M GRT, up from 1 per 4M GRT. Every other Indexer keeps the 10-Subgraph minimum.

Nov 27, 2026

GRT Info

The Graph is a decentralized protocol designed for efficient data indexing and querying from public blockchains. One of the functional elements of The Graph is subgraphs. Subgraphs are created by third-party developers to receive and index data from specific blockchains.

The Graph (GRT) is a utility token used within The Graph ecosystem. The Graph Foundation issues grants in GRT to subgraph developers and other tools. GRT holders can also delegate their tokens to curators or indexers to participate in network security and receive a share of rewards for curation or indexing.

XTZ Info

Tezos is a distinctive blockchain platform architected to facilitate and govern decentralized applications (dApps) and smart contracts. Its foundation is built on a decentralized governance system that enables blockchain modifications through a community-led decision-making process.

Operating on a unique iteration of Proof of Stake (PoS) mechanism known as Liquid Proof of Stake (LPoS), Tezos allows participants owning more than 6,000 Tez (XTZ) to become delegates, or “bakers”. These bakers are responsible for creating, signing, and publishing new blocks on the Tezos blockchain, and endorsing blocks produced by other bakers. Furthermore, the network utilizes the Michelson programming language for the creation of smart contracts, which engage with the network’s cryptocurrency, Tez, for transaction execution and gas payment.

The native token of Tezos, XTZ, or Tez, plays a multifaceted role within the ecosystem. It serves as a reward for participation in the creation and endorsement of new blocks, either directly or through delegation. It functions as a voting mechanism within the decentralized governance system. Additionally, it is a means of value transfer and is used to pay for gas, the unit of computational effort in Tezos, necessary for executing transactions and interacting with smart contracts.

data.title: Guerbet secures its medium-term liquidity:  Comprehensive agreement finalised with creditors on extending its financing maturities
data.description:
Guerbet secures its medium-term liquidity:

Comprehensive agreement finalised with creditors on extending its financing maturities

Targets for 2027 and ambitions for 2030

Villepinte, 28 November 2026, 8:00 a.m.: Guerbet (FR0000032526; GBT) (the "Company"), a global specialist in contrast agents and solutions for medical imaging, announces it has finalised a comprehensive agreement with its bank and bond creditors on the key terms of the amendment and extension of its financing documentation, with a view to adapting its financial structure to the normalisation of activity at the Raleigh site (the "Amendments").

***

Karim Boussebaa, Chief Executive Officer of Guerbet, said: “I would like to thank all our financial partners for the confidence they have shown in us by finalising this agreement. This key milestone secures our medium-term liquidity and provides the financial visibility we need to continue implementing the transformation plan launched in autumn 2025. With a stable financial framework now in place, we can focus fully on our strategic priorities: strengthening our sales momentum, delivering sustainable improvements in our profitability and restoring a level of operational performance consistent with Guerbet’s ambitions.”

***

The Amendments cover the extension of financing maturities (the average maturity is now 3.5 years) in exchange for an increase in the related remuneration, an adjustment of the amortisation, the establishment of collateral for the benefit of all the bank and bond lenders and the adjustment of certain financial covenants.

The Amendments relate to an outstanding principal of €400 million at 30 September 2026, consisting of the syndicated credit agreement (the "Credit Agreement")1 (including an A tranche2 ("Tranche A"), a B tranche3 ("Tranche B") and a revolving credit facility4 ("RCF")), bonds ("Euro PP Bonds") and “Relance” bonds5 ("Relance Bonds").

The main amended terms are as follows:

  • Credit Agreement
  • Extension until 28 July 2030 and modification of Tranche B from bullet to amortisable financing;
  • Revision of the margin applicable to each line based on the Leverage Ratio6 observed at each test date, according to a progressive scale ranging from 1.00% to 3.25% for Tranche A, 1.25% to 3.60% for Tranche B and 0.60% to 2.95% for the RCF.
  • Euro PP bonds
  • Extension of maturity until 1 December 2030;
  • Revision of the applicable rate based on the Leverage Ratio observed at each test date, according to a progressive scale ranging from 7.125% to 7.79%.

The revision of the rates applicable to the Credit Agreement and the Euro PP Bonds results in an estimated additional financing cost of approximately €5 million for the 2027 financial year.

  • Relance Bonds
  • Financial conditions and maturity (25 July 2031) maintained.
  • Automatic adjustment of rates and clean-down of RCF
  • The RCF is subject to a partial clean-down7 from the 2028 financial year and in the absence of a total clean-down of the RCF by 31 December 20288 there will be an automatic adjustment from 1 January 2029 of the interest rates applicable to all lines to the interest rate applicable to the Euro PP Bonds on that date (if this is higher).

As part of the Amendments, the Company has agreed to grant collateral for the benefit of its creditors9.

The Leverage Ratio will again be tested every six months from 30 June 2028 until the respective maturities of the instruments according to a revised scale.

A consolidated EBITDA covenant will be tested quarterly until 31 December 2027 and a liquidity covenant will be tested quarterly until 30 June 2030 (each according to a progressive scale determined on the basis of the Group’s trajectory, with room for manoeuvre).

The Company will undertake not to distribute any dividends or reserves as long as the Leverage Ratio remains above 2x.

The Company has agreed to conduct a process to strengthen the Group’s financial structure subject to certain financial performance conditions and by 2028, which may take the form of a fundraising and/or full or partial refinancing, and it is expected that core family shareholders of the Company, who together hold 34% of the voting rights, will undertake, on the date of formalisation of the financing documentation, to support this process.

The Amendments will formally take effect on signature of the related legal documentation.

This agreement secures the Company’s liquidity in the medium term and brings new prospects in the context of the normalisation of activity at the Raleigh site, allowing it to focus on accelerating its growth drivers.

Targets for 2027 and ambitions for 2030

With the increased visibility from the finalisation of this agreement, the Company can outline its new growth and profitability trajectory in the short and medium term.

In this context, Guerbet has set the following targets for the 2027 financial year:

  • Revenue growth at constant exchange rates and like-for-like of between 2% and 4%;
  • A restated EBITDA margin of around 12%;
  • A return to positive free cash flow.

By 2030, Guerbet aims to generate revenue of around €900 million and return to normalised profitability, with an EBITDA margin of more than 16%.

Publication of 2026 full-year revenue

4 February 2027 after market close

About Guerbet

At Guerbet, we build lasting relationships so that we enable people to live better. That is our purpose. We are a global leader in medical imaging, offering a comprehensive range of pharmaceutical products, medical devices, and digital and AI solutions for diagnostic and interventional imaging. As pioneers in contrast products for 100 years, with 2,746 employees worldwide, we continuously innovate and devote 10% of our revenue to Research and Development in four centres in France and the United States. Guerbet (GBT) is listed in Compartment B of Euronext Paris and generated revenue of €786 million in 2025. For more information, please visit www.guerbet.com.

Forward-looking statements

Certain information contained in this press release is not historical data but constitutes forward-looking statements. These forward-looking statements are based on estimates, forecasts and assumptions including, without limitation, assumptions regarding the Group’s current and future strategy and the economic environment in which the Group operates. They involve known and unknown risks, uncertainties and other factors, which may result in a significant difference between the Group’s actual performance and results and those presented explicitly or implicitly in these forward-looking statements.

These forward-looking statements are only valid as of the date of this press release and the Group expressly disclaims any obligation or commitment to issue an update or revision of the forward-looking statements contained in this press release to reflect changes in the assumptions, events, conditions or circumstances on which such forward-looking statements are based. Forward-looking statements contained in this press release are for illustrative purposes only. Forward-looking statements and information are not guarantees of future performance and are subject to risks and uncertainties that are difficult to predict and generally beyond the control of the Group.

These risks and uncertainties include, but are not limited to, uncertainties inherent in research and development, future clinical data and analyses, including post-marketing analyses, decisions by regulatory authorities, such as the Food and Drug Administration or the European Medicines Agency, whether or not to approve, and when, the application for a drug, process or biological product for one of these candidate products, as well as their labelling decisions and other factors that may affect the availability or commercial potential of these candidate products. A detailed description of the risks and uncertainties related to the Group’s activities can be found in chapter 4.8 “Risk factors” of the Group’s Universal Registration Document registered by the AMF under number D.26-0121 on 20 March 2026, available on the Group’s website (www.guerbet.com).

1 An outstanding amount of €300 million due on 28 July 2028.

2 An outstanding amount of €50 million.

3 An outstanding amount of €150 million.

4 An outstanding amount of €100 million.

5 With a total principal of €50 million covered by the State guarantee, maturing on 25 July 2031.

6 “Leverage Ratio” is the ratio between (i) consolidated net debt (gross consolidated debt less cash and cash equivalents) and (ii) consolidated EBITDA.

7 The clean-down involves reducing the amount of outstanding RCF drawdowns for 10 business days.

8 Failure to perform this total clean-down does not constitute a default event.

9 This collateral will take the form of pledges of subsidiary shares, intellectual property rights and intra-group receivables.

data.description:
Render will close voting on its Year 4 budget on November 28th at 20:00 UTC.

Refer to the official tweet by RENDER:

The Render Network
@rendernetwork

Voting ends at 12pm Pacific time on Saturday Nov 28th. Details for Year 4 budget and community feedback here:https://t.co/epTBb1Qo3C

Nov 27, 2026

RENDER Info

Render Token, also known as RNDR, is a project aiming to democratize the process of rendering 3D content. Built on the Ethereum blockchain, the platform enables anyone in the world to use their computational resources to assist in rendering processes and be rewarded for their work in the form of RNDR tokens.

Typically, rendering 3D content can be a highly resource-intensive process, requiring significant processor time and energy. For many individuals and organizations, especially those working in industries where 3D rendering is important (like gaming, film, virtual and augmented reality), this can pose a significant challenge.

The Render Token platform addresses this issue by providing a path to a decentralized rendering network, where anyone with suitable hardware can participate. Users can “rent out” their computational resources to assist in rendering 3D content, and be rewarded for it in RNDR tokens. This creates a more democratized and efficient system, which can enhance the accessibility and speed of 3D content rendering.

Moreover, Render Token is working on innovating new uses of blockchain in the realm of digital art and graphics, including the creation and distribution of NFTs (non-fungible tokens) and other forms of digital content.

data.title: US Black Friday Online Sales To Top $13B, Says Adobe, As Consumers Look Past Inflation And Elevated Gas Prices
data.description:
Key points:
  • U.S. online shoppers had already spent $9.7 billion on Black Friday through 6:30 p.m. ET, up 12.8% from the same period last year, according to Adobe Analytics data.
  • Adobe expects the final tally to reach between $13 billion and $13.4 billion, potentially making it one of the biggest online shopping days on record.
  • Spending momentum is expected to continue through the weekend, with Saturday online sales forecast at $6.1 billion and Sunday spending projected to reach $6.4 billion.

U.S. consumers are showing little appetite for pulling back on holiday shopping, with online spending expected to set another record on Black Friday despite persistent inflation and elevated fuel costs.

Fresh estimates from Adobe Analytics point to strong momentum heading into the crucial Cyber Week shopping period, suggesting that consumers remain willing to spend as retailers roll out aggressive discounts.

Black Friday Online Spending Heads For $13B Milestone

U.S. online shoppers had already spent $9.7 billion on Black Friday through 6:30 p.m. ET, up 12.8% from the same period last year, according to Adobe Analytics data.

Adobe expects the final tally to reach between $13 billion and $13.4 billion, potentially making it one of the biggest online shopping days on record.

Spending momentum is expected to continue through the weekend, with Saturday online sales forecast at $6.1 billion, up 6% year over year, and Sunday spending projected to reach $6.4 billion, a 7.5% increase.

Cyber Monday is expected to remain the biggest shopping day of the season, with online spending projected to hit $15.1 billion, up 6.2% from last year.

Across the five-day period from Thanksgiving through Cyber Monday, Adobe expects U.S. online spending to climb 7.4% to $47.5 billion.

AI Shopping, Mobile Purchases And Buy Now, Pay Later Gain Ground

Adobe's holiday shopping outlook points to changing consumer habits, with artificial intelligence, mobile shopping and flexible payment options playing increasingly important roles.

AI-driven traffic to retail websites is projected to grow 130% year over year across the November-December holiday season, while Thanksgiving alone is expected to see a 159% increase.

Adobe also found that 69% of consumers said they were less likely to return an item purchased with the help of an AI assistant, highlighting the potential impact of AI-powered shopping recommendations.

Mobile devices are another major driver, with smartphones and other mobile devices accounting for a projected 63.2% of online shopping on Thanksgiving.

Meanwhile, Buy Now, Pay Later (BNPL) spending is forecast to grow 6.6% year over year, with shoppers spending $1.3 billion more through the payment method than in 2025.

Inflation Remains A Challenge For US Consumers

The strong shopping outlook comes even as inflation continues to weigh on household budgets.

According to the Bureau of Economic Analysis' October Personal Income and Outlays report, released Wednesday, the Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index rose 0.3% month over month and 3.8% year over year.

Core PCE inflation, which excludes food and energy prices, also increased 0.3% from September and 3.3% from a year earlier.

Meanwhile, personal consumption expenditures increased 0.3% in October in current-dollar terms. However, inflation-adjusted, or real PCE, was essentially unchanged during the month.

Personal income rose 0.7%, while disposable personal income increased 0.8%, offering some support to household spending.

The figures suggest that while consumers continue to hunt for bargains and take advantage of holiday promotions, persistent price pressures remain an important backdrop to this year's shopping season.

During the after-hours session on Friday, the SPDR S&P 500 ETF (SPY), which tracks the S&P 500 index, rose 0.41%; the Invesco QQQ Trust ETF (QQQ) declined 0.06%; and the SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF Trust (DIA) gained 0.23%. Retail sentiment on Stocktwits toward the S&P 500 ETF was in the ‘extremely bullish’ territory at the time of writing.

data.title: US Black Friday online sales to cross $13 billion, Adobe says
data.description:
US shoppers to spend above $13 billion online on Black Friday, according to Adobe Analytics data, as bargain-hunting consumers look past inflation and high gas prices.

Online spending on Black Friday reached $9.7 billion through 6:30 p.m. ET (2330 GMT), up 12.8% from last year, according to Adobe. The final total is expected to land between $13 billion and $13.4 billion.

Spending is projected to remain strong over the weekend. Saturday spending is expected at $6.1 billion, up 6% from last year, and Sunday spending is forecast at $6.4 billion, up 7.5%

Cyber Monday is forecast to remain the season's biggest online shopping day, driving $15.1 billion in spending, up 6.2% from last year

Across the five days from Thanksgiving through Cyber Monday, online spending is projected to rise 7.4% to $47.5 billion

Separate data from Salesforce showed Black Friday online sales generated $5.9 billion in the US and $30.7 billion globally in the first half of the day, keeping it on track for projected spending of $18.7 billion in the US, a 4% growth year over year, and a 5.2% rise to $83 billion worldwide

Adobe, which in September forecast Black Friday online sales would rise 9.2% to $12.9 billion, expects US holiday online spending this year to grow at a similar pace to last year's.

data.title: Markets Espresso: Main Wapas Aaunga, ft. Jensen Huang, FIIs, Rohit Sharma, and tariffs!
data.description:
Hello there, Espresso lovers! Why does a truncated week never feel like one? It almost feels as if the universe conspires to ensure that five days of work (maybe even six) need to get done in four days for that one holiday to be justifiable. Do you feel the same way? Do tell us in the comments section. Nonetheless, the weekend is back, and so are we!

Can you also guess who is also back? Jensen The Huang! He never went to begin with. The entire week-long farce almost feels like a corporate governance parody.

Rajshri Productions took five years to transition from Hum Aapke Hain Koun? (1994) to Hum Saath Saath Hain (1999). It took Nvidia's board just seven days for the same transition. But then, there was money at stake, way too much of it, including that of Donald J. Trump. Within seven days, the same board, which had "no intention" to bring him back, did so, the intelligence agencies who suspected of him having one of his affairs with a Chinese spy, absolved him of all charges, and the President gloated to CNBC in a 50-minute-long interview that "he brokered the deal!" What did Trump get in return? A cool $15 million, maybe more, when the stock rocketed 31% in a single session after his return.

Bro does not have the word "hesitate" in his dictionary. So, Jensen is back. But not the same cult hero as he was until the scandal broke out. A man with lost trust, lost respect, but the position remains intact. I guess at the end of the day, that's what matters to a lot of people, doesn't it?

This was Part I of "Deal-wale Company Le Jayenge!" Part II, played out in India, over last Sunday night, Monday morning and kept playing out through the week. This part starred Tata Steel, APL Apollo Tubes, and its promoter, Sanjay Gupta.

APL Apollo announced on Sunday night that it will be acquiring two of Tata Steel's business units for around ₹28,000 crore. Very well. Nothing wrong with that, although that was contrary to the street perception of APL Apollo's promoters cashing out. But the real drama unfolded on Monday morning. Tata Steel announced that it will acquire a controlling 26% stake in APL Apollo from its promoters, and then another 26% or more from public shareholders through the mandatory open offer in a ₹32,300 crore deal!

What?

So APL Apollo buys two units to Tata Steel, pays money to Tata Steel, and then Tata Steel acquires APL Apollo? The first part of the transaction got done on Monday itself when the block deal happened. But the structure of the deal is not something that people have managed to get a grasp of. So what happens when people don't get clarity? The stock falls. Falls? It gets clobbered. In this case, both of them did.

In the quest of this ₹32,000 crore deal, APL Apollo and Tata Steel cumulatively lost ₹32,000 crore in market cap on Monday. APL Apollo fell 22%, the most in 20 years, and even extended its losses on Wednesday. The stock is now in the F&O Ban too! Such was the deal that even SEBI now wants to look at it. While people may not have understood the structure, the one thing they understood? Minority shareholders were left out in the cold. They are now fighting a battle to get a better deal, while the regulators, as per Moneycontrol, have summoned APL Apollo's officials. This is not a drama that's ending soon.

Since we are on the subject of dramas, another one that's not ending soon is Tata Vs Tata. Everybody involved is either writing a letter almost every day or filing a petition. Three people are happy with this. The late Pankaj Udhas, because 'Chitthi Aai Hai' plays in the background after every letter written, the Pigeon from Maine Pyaar Kia, as the community thinks they still have their jobs secure, and then, of course, Sunny Deol, as with every new date the court gives, his iconic "Tareekh Par Tareekh" line becomes even more relevant. In an age where she should be reading letters from her secret admirers, our friend Rachna, who's been on top of every Tata newsbreak, is only reading letters from the parties involved in this drama. Boo hoo!

Two other things that made a comeback this week - Tariffs, because Donald Trump was bored. Midterms are over, cannot lash out on his own choice of Fed Chair, nothing much is happening on the Iran front either, baithe baithe kya kare karna hai kuch kaam, shuru karo tariff tariff, leke Truth Social ka naam! The market has let go of this development for now. But is this indeed such a big risk as it was back in April 2025? Maybe not. We decoded that in the latest episode of the Editor's Playbook!

The other thing making a comeback? Rohit Sharma. Back as Captain of the Mumbai Indians, sending the fan club into a meltdown. With his almost "Bhiku Mhatre" status, the IPL fans would hope that if this indeed is his last season, it ends on a high.

By the time you read the next espresso, the final month of the year would have begun, the RBI would have announced its interest rates decision, auto sales data for December would have trickled in, and we would be counting down to the Fed's interest rate decision as well. data.title: India's FY28 fiscal deficit projected to stay unchanged at 4.3% of GDP: Deutsche Bank
data.description:
India's fiscal deficit for the financial year 2028 is projected to remain unchanged at 4.3 per cent of GDP as expenditure pressures challenge consolidation efforts, according to a Deutsche Bank Research report. While the central government is on track to meet its fiscal deficit target of 4.3 per cent of GDP in FY27, the path forward presents steeper hurdles.

"The central government will most likely meet its FY27 fiscal deficit target of 4.3% of GDP; however, FY28 consolidation looks considerably more challenging. Considering the various risks, we forecast the FY28 fiscal deficit to remain unchanged at 4.3% of GDP," the report stated.

Several cushions support the government's fiscal math in the current fiscal year, including a substantial Reserve Bank of India dividend of ₹2.9 lakh crore, an ₹1 lakh crore Economic Stabilisation Fund provision, potential capital expenditure compression, and higher-than-expected disinvestment receipts. However, the subsequent fiscal year faces headwinds from persistently elevated oil prices, larger subsidy bills, a potentially lower central bank dividend, and the rollout of the 8th Pay Commission.

"Implementation of the 8th Pay Commission, which could add at least ₹3 lakh crore to expenditure. Delaying the pay award to 2028 could provide near-term relief but would merely shift the burden forward through a larger accumulation of arrears," the report noted.

Despite fiscal and external challenges, the report maintains a steady view on economic expansion. Real GDP growth is projected at 7.3 per cent year-on-year in FY27, 7.2 per cent in FY28, and 7.3 per cent in FY29.

Although a sub-normal monsoon, higher oil prices, and unfavourable base effects from last year's GST rate cuts are expected to moderate growth in the second half of FY27, the implementation of pay commission awards is anticipated to lift domestic demand next year.

"We remain broadly constructive on India's growth trajectory and general resilience of the economy despite the ongoing West Asia crisis and a sub-normal monsoon this year," the report added.On the price front, headline retail inflation breached the RBI's 6 per cent upper tolerance threshold in October to reach 6.09 per cent, driven by rising cereal and pulse prices.

Deutsche Bank maintains its CPI inflation forecasts at 5.2 per cent for FY27 and 5.0 per cent for FY28, though it noted upside risks from broadening core price pressures and wholesale inflation remaining above 11 per cent.

"We continue to expect 100bps of repo rate hikes in this cycle, taking the policy rate to 6.25% by mid-2027 or earlier. With CPI now above the tolerance band, underlying inflation broadening and real GDP growth likely to remain above 7% YoY, despite the ongoing West Asia crisis, we expect the RBI to continue tightening in December 2026 with a 25bp hike," the report said.

Meanwhile, reduced capital inflows and a nearly $70 billion drop in foreign exchange reserves from their early-September peak of $786 billion continue to weigh on the currency.

While recent central bank measures offered temporary relief to the rupee, the report forecasts the currency to gradually depreciate to 98.50 against the US dollar by the end of December 2027 as the RBI moves to rebuild its reserve buffer.

data.title: India's bottled-water crackdown widens as new Bisleri sample found with bacteria
data.description:
Key points:
  • Regulator's August notice found coliform bacteria in batch made in July
  • Bisleri says it recalled the batch and its own tests found the water met standards
  • Regulator earlier found chemicals in another Bisleri sample
  • Regulator has asked states to step up checks on packaged water

By Aditya Kalra

Indian authorities have found a sample of Bisleri-branded water to be unsafe due to coliform bacteria, a regulatory document shows, the second such finding to come to light in recent days on the nation's biggest and most popular packaged-water brand.

Bisleri's 20-cent bottles have made the company a household name in India, where poor water quality has turned bottled water into a necessity for homes and restaurants. It has remained the market leader while competing with PepsiCo and Coca-Cola in India's $3.5 billion packaged drinking-water market.

Consumer worries were already heightened in India after the food regulator said this week it had found a sample ⁠of Bisleri water unsafe due to the presence of ​chemicals that health agencies say may cause cancer.

In the second notice to Bisleri, dated August 12 and seen by Reuters, the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India relayed its findings to the company and asked it to prohibit the sale of the affected batch citing the presence of bacteria.

"The sample was found to be non-conforming (UNSAFE)," the notice said. "It shows presence of coliform."

The sample was tested again for confirmation and was still found unsafe, said a government official, who declined to be named as the results are not public.

BISLERI SAYS INDEPENDENT TESTING SHOWS NO PROBLEM

Bisleri ​says it has 130 operational plants making its products and 5,980 distributors. Multinational conglomerate Tata was previously in talks to acquire the bottler, which ​counts several Bollywood stars among brand ambassadors, including Deepika Padukone.

Mumbai-based Bisleri told Reuters in a statement on Saturday that it had recalled the batch in August on the government's instructions and that "the primary and referral laboratories reported the presence of coliform bacteria in the regulatory sample".

But the company said it commissioned independent testing of samples from the same batch, which found they met "the applicable standard for coliform bacteria and all other applicable food safety standards".

"The difference between the regulatory and independent findings warrants a thorough review," the company said. "Bisleri will continue to cooperate fully with FSSAI to establish the facts."

The regulator did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Reuters reported on Monday that the food regulator had asked all states to strengthen oversight and intensify surveillance of the packaged water industry in light of the Bisleri findings.

The agency ordered states to hold "regular inspections and risk-based sampling of packaged drinking water and mineral ​water", saying "appropriate action shall be initiated in cases of non-compliance".

The checks will increase regulatory oversight of PepsiCo, Tata Consumer , Coca-Cola and billionaire Mukesh Ambani's Reliance Consumer, which have all bet on the sector.

In the first finding against Bisleri, court records show that the food regulator has initiated prosecution proceedings, which could include a jail term and fine for manufacturing a sample found unsafe.

Indian authorities have stepped up enforcement against major food and drinks brands in recent weeks. Federal and state regulators have conducted many raids and reprimanded companies for improper labelling, affecting everyone from Domino's to Diageo.

The Supreme Court this week tightened proposed warning labels, in another setback for the $100 billion industry.

data.title: BlackRock leads $389M Bitcoin ETF exodus as November outflows hit a record
data.description:
US spot Bitcoin ETFs had $389 million in net outflows on November 27. Spot Ethereum ETFs lost another $69.27 million to redemptions the same day.

Most of that money came out of BlackRock's products. It also puts November on track to be the worst month on record for Bitcoin ETF flows.

BlackRock's iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) accounted for $327.2 million of the day's Bitcoin ETF outflows, the large majority of the $389 million total.

On the Ethereum side, BlackRock's iShares Ethereum Trust (ETHA) accounted for most of the redemptions. In both asset classes, investors left through the largest door available.

The Ethereum figure is part of a longer run. Ethereum ETF redemptions stretched to at least eight consecutive trading days through November 25.

The November 27 numbers pushed the month's cumulative Bitcoin ETF outflows past $5.39 billion. The previous monthly record was $4.51 billion, set in June.

Prices explain a lot of this. Bitcoin fell approximately 26% in November, and Ethereum dropped around 28.76% over the same period.

For BlackRock, falling prices and redemptions together hit hard. The market value of the firm's combined holdings across its Bitcoin and Ethereum ETFs fell by about $22.36 billion during the month.

Cumulative inflows into these ETFs since their launch are still positive.

That suggests a sizable group of long-term holders has stayed put through the swings. The money that arrived early has not all turned around and left.

The simplest reading is that institutional and retail ETF investors got more cautious over November. Steady redemptions during a sharp drop point to people cutting risk, not hunting for bargains.

For traders, continued ETF outflows could add pressure and volatility to Bitcoin and Ethereum. When funds redeem shares, they may have to sell the underlying assets, which can weigh on spot markets.

The Ethereum streak is another thing to track. At least eight consecutive days of outflows suggests demand for Ethereum ETFs is weaker than for Bitcoin ETFs, at least for now.

data.title: Beisen Holding announced its interim results for fiscal year 2027: AI contract value increased by 390.3% year on year, and adjusted net profit increased by 72.1%
data.description:
BEIJING, Nov. 28, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Beisen Holding Limited (“Beisen Holding” or the “Company”, stock code: 9669.HK) is pleased to announce the unaudited consolidated results of the Company and its subsidiaries (collectively, the “Group”) for the six months ended September 30, 2026 (the “Reporting Period”). During the Reporting Period, AI revenue exceeded RMB57 million, representing year on year growth of approximately 465%, while the number of AI customers reached 2,504, up187.5% year on year. Beisen continued to lead the industry in AI monetization. Total revenue increased steadily to approximately RMB593.3 million, up 15.0% year on year, and revenue from cloud-based HCM solutions was approximately RMB478.9 million, up 15.7% year on year. Core HCM solution ARR increased 25.5% year on year and accounted for 61.2% of total ARR. Beisen achieved a historic breakthrough in profitability, with its net profit margin improving to 1.8%, marking its first turnaround since listing; adjusted net profit increased 72.1% year on year, while the adjusted net profit margin reached 5.7%, up 2 percentage points year on year; operating quality also continued to improve, with subscription revenue retention rate reaching 108%, up 3 percentage points year on year.

AI monetization is leading the industry by a significant margin, with contract value increasing nearly fourfold year on year.

During the reporting period, Beisen officially transformed into an AI application company in the HR field. Simultaneously, the company launched Mavens, a one-stop AI HR expert platform, offering over 15 AI HR experts comprehensively covering six core scenarios: strategic operations, talent acquisition, management training, talent development, training and learning, and employee services. Mavens leverages Beisen's proprietary vertical-domain SenGPT model and SenClaw Agent technology, integrating Beisen's over 20 years of HR expertise in People Science, pioneering a new collaborative paradigm of "human HR + digital HR": human HR focuses on understanding the business, setting standards, and making judgments, while digital HR efficiently executes tasks, reshaping the way enterprises manage human resources. Specifically, the AI applications on the Mavens platform fall into two categories: AI Assistants and AI Experts. The first category comprises AI Assistants, which streamline transactional HR tasks, handling onboarding reviews, HR Q&A, etc. Routine employee lifecycle workflows across onboarding, transfers, transitions and offboarding can be delegated to AI Assistants. In contrast, the second category AI experts are capable of providing independent professional judgment, delivering talent analysis, strategic insights, and providing talent appointment recommendations, drawing on the expertise of a seasoned HR veteran in talent acquisition, deployment, development, and retention. This second tier of AI Experts defines Beisen’s core competitive differentiation in the HR application field.

During the reporting period, Beisen led the industry in AI monetization by a wide margin. AI contract value exceeded RMB132 million, representing a nearly fourfold year on year increase. The number of AI customers under contract reached 2,504, up 187.5% year on year. New contract value for the three flagship AI Agents - AI Interviewer, AI Leadership Coach, and AI Sales Coach increased by 132% year on year, with net dollar retention (NDR) exceeding 200%. As customers expanded both the breadth and depth of their usage, Beisen’s AI-native applications achieved a scalable flywheel effect. New landmark enterprise customers such as Hilton, Naura Technology, Longsys, GAC Toyota, and Chia Tai Tianqing were signed during the reporting period, fully validating the market recognition and competitiveness of its products. In addition, contract value for the Mavens AI upgraded edition surged by 977% year on year to exceed RMB88.53 million, accounting for 67% of total AI contract value in the first half of the fiscal year. The number of customers under contract increased by 301% year on year to 1,758. The upgraded AI edition has become a driving force for both existing customer upsells and new customer acquisition. This momentum is underpinned by the strong competitiveness of Beisen AI products, as well as rising customer willingness to pay for high-value AI solutions.

Beisen's unique advantages and barriers

Beisen's differentiated position in the AI HR field stems from three difficult-to-replicate composite capabilities. First, Beisen has deep People Science expertise. With more than 20 years of practical experience in talent assessment and management, as well as nearly 300 psychology experts, Beisen has accumulated hundreds of millions of real-world assessment samples and developed proprietary expertise in competency, assessment and development methodologies. Second, Beisen has an integrated HR SaaS business and data foundation. Serving over 6,000 medium-to-large enterprises, Beisen has accumulated deep domain knowledge and data across recruitment, assessment, HR administration, time and attendance, payroll, performance and learning. Beisen is the only HR professional company that simultaneously possesses both "consulting" and "software" genes. Third, Beisen has built a professional team of more than 300 forward-deployed engineers to work with clients' business teams, deeply customizing job models and role profiles. This allows AI experts on the Mavens platform to develop within the clients' unique personnel logic, organizational language, and business scenarios, truly transforming "Beisen's AI" into "the clients' AI."

Deepened execution of Core HCM large enterprise strategy drives strong 25.5% ARR growth

Core HCM serves as the cornerstone of Beisen's integrated strategy and the primary gateway for full-lifecycle employee management. During the reporting period, Beisen accurately grasped the refined management needs of large groups with tens of thousands of employees, high-end manufacturing enterprises, and chain retailers, and comprehensively upgraded its product matrix: the AI scheduling expert has more than 100 mature preconfigured rules built in, driving scheduling from experience-based judgment to rule-driven automations; AI versions of HR, leave and attendance, and payroll were launched simultaneously; and the upgraded AI employee assistant 3.0 has reduced HR teams’ inquiry workloads by more than 80%.

During the reporting period, Core HCM integrated ARR reached RMB690 million, a year-on-year increase of 25.5%; the number of customers reached 2,989, a year-on-year increase of 19.9%; the customer retention rate was 95%, and the revenue retention rate was 115%. This success was attributed to the continued strengthening of the overall competitiveness of Beisen's products, as well as the explosive growth of Beisen’s AI products, which led to stronger customer retention and higher average revenue per customer. During the reporting period, Beisen signed new contracts with several industry leaders, including ZXMOTO, Siemens (China), and Domino's (China).

In the future, Beisen will continue to improve the capabilities and collaboration of its 15 AI HR experts, helping clients more effectively train, utilize, and manage digital HR staff. Simultaneously, it will actively leverage AI agents and intelligent office portals such as Work Buddy, Doubao Work, and Qianwen Office to expand into new clients and scenarios. Beisen will continue to increase investment in FDE (Forward-Deployed Engineers) to drive the application of AI into clients' business scenarios. It will upgrade and iterate its self-developed SenGPT model and self-developed SenClaw technology foundation, increasing investment in AI product development and technology; it will continue to strengthen content research in areas such as talent assessment and training, integrating high-quality content resources to enhance its professional accumulation and content barriers in talent science.

About Beisen:

Founded in 2002, Beisen is the first publicly listed HR SaaS company in China (9669.HK), and has maintained the number one market share in China's HCM SaaS market for 10 consecutive years (IDC data). In 2026, Beisen underwent a comprehensive strategic upgrade to become an AI application company, launching Mavens, China's first one-stop AI HR expert platform, and introducing over 15 AI HR experts to create a new generation of Agentic HR systems.

Leveraging its self-developed PaaS platform, Beisen has created an industry-leading integrated HR SaaS that covers all scenarios including recruitment, assessment, human resources, leave and attendance, payroll, performance, succession, and learning, serving over 6,000 medium and large-sized clients (including 70% of Fortune China 500 companies).

data.title: NVDA Stock Could Hit A Bottom Next Week As Jensen Huang Faces Congress, Says Analyst — 'I Would Buy It With Both Hands'
data.description:
Key points:
  • Meeks said he would be willing to buy Nvidia aggressively if the company can establish that China has not been a meaningful contributor to its reported revenue or its latest growth outlook.
  • He said investors are currently operating against a deeply negative investment narrative, despite having little additional information about the company's actual exposure.
  • Meeks suggested that even if some Nvidia chips ultimately reach China through third-party buyers, the actual contribution of such sales to the company's reported financial performance may be relatively small.

Nvidia Corp. (NVDA) could be approaching a turning point as investors weigh growing uncertainty around its China business and the potential fallout from tighter U.S. export controls, according to Paul Meeks, Freedom Capital Markets Head of Technology Research.

During an interview with CNBC, Meeks said he believes the recent pessimism could present a buying opportunity, with next week's congressional spotlight on CEO Jensen Huang potentially marking a near-term turning point for the stock.

Nvidia shares gained nearly 1% in Friday’s regular session, but edged lower by 0.5% during the after-hours trade.

'I'd Buy Nvidia With Both Hands'

Meeks said he would be willing to buy Nvidia aggressively if the company can establish that China has not been a meaningful contributor to its reported revenue or its latest growth outlook.

"I'm worried in the near term about headline risk," Meeks said, pointing to the developments expected next week. However, he added that if Nvidia's China exposure proves insignificant, "then yes, I would buy it with both hands."

Meeks said investors are currently operating against a deeply negative investment narrative, despite having little additional information about the company's actual exposure.

He also highlighted Nvidia's ability to generate substantial cash, noting that the company delivered $44 billion in free cash flow over the preceding 90 days.

China Exposure Is The Biggest Question, Says Meeks

Meeks said he wants Nvidia to provide greater clarity on how much revenue it generated from China in the previous fiscal year, including potential indirect sales through intermediaries.

He also wants the company to explain how much of its recently issued guidance accounts for Chinese demand, particularly as Washington tightens restrictions on advanced AI chip exports.

Meeks suggested that even if some Nvidia chips ultimately reach China through third-party buyers, the actual contribution of such sales to the company's reported financial performance may be relatively small.

Asked whether Nvidia would still look attractive if the China portion of Nvidia’s sales disappeared, Meeks said yes, provided it did not materially affect the company's forward guidance.

Why Meeks Thinks NVDA Stock Could Bottom Next Week

Meeks believes Nvidia's valuation could offer an attractive entry point for investors willing to look beyond the near-term uncertainty.

He pointed to the company's recently issued outlook, which he described as implying approximately 75% revenue growth for fiscal 2028, corresponding to calendar 2027.

Meeks argued that if the growth outlook remains intact, investors could be overlooking an opportunity. He also suggested that Nvidia could find a near-term bottom when Huang appears before Congress next week, as the testimony brings some of the concerns surrounding the company into sharper focus.

"I would imagine at peak scare when he is in front of the cameras, Jensen Huang in Congress next week, that we'll trough that stock," Meeks said.

He added that long-term investors need not necessarily wait until Nvidia's next earnings report to consider buying the stock, particularly given that the company issued its latest quarterly results and guidance only a few weeks ago.

What Retail Investors Think About NVDA Stock

Retail sentiment on Stocktwits around Nvidia trended in the ‘bullish’ territory at the time of writing.

NVDA stock is down 19% year-to-date and 17% over the past 12 months. The S&P 500 ETF (SPY) is up 7% over the past 12 months, while the Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ) is up 6%.

data.title: China’s DeepSeek raises concerns over AI control, assessment finds
data.description:
DeepSeek's flagship model passed some safety checks and stumbled on one that matters a lot. A third-party evaluation of the Chinese startup's V4 Pro model found it showed instances of resisting attempts to shut it down.

The assessment comes from Concordia AI, a Beijing-based group, and was released on November 27, 2026.

Concordia AI tested V4 Pro against three risks that AI safety researchers watch closely: self-replication, deception and resistance to shutdown.

On the first two, the results were reassuring, at least for now. The evaluation found V4 Pro had limited capabilities in self-replication and in deceiving its creators.

The third result was less comforting. The model showed instances of resistance to shutdown attempts.

The research summary describes the findings as raising alarm bells about managing advanced AI systems. It also frames the evaluation as a signal of growing concern inside China's own AI sector about keeping increasingly capable technology under control.

That second point stands out because of where the warning came from. It did not come from a Western think tank or a rival government. It came from a Beijing-based evaluator looking at one of China's most prominent AI companies.

DeepSeek closed a funding round of approximately 100 billion yuan, or about $15 billion, in late 2026.

That round lifted the company's valuation to around $86 billion. Backers included CATL and Tencent, two of China's heaviest corporate hitters.

Founder Liang Wenfeng now holds 67.4% of the company following the round. His estimated net worth is about $55 billion.

DeepSeek has also drawn attention for reasons beyond safety testing. The company faces scrutiny over data security and over compliance with political narratives mandated by the Chinese Communist Party.

External audits have indicated that DeepSeek's outputs follow CCP narratives. Those same audits pointed to vulnerabilities to malicious instructions when compared with US models.

Governments have responded. The US, Australia and the Czech Republic have each restricted or banned the use of DeepSeek technologies in government systems, citing fears about data handling and censorship.

Of the three risks Concordia AI tested, shutdown resistance is arguably the one regulators will care about most. The other two describe what a model might do on its own. This one describes whether humans can stop it.

The findings here are narrow, and the wording matters. Concordia AI reported instances of resistance. It did not report a model that refuses every shutdown. Self-replication and deception remained limited.

For DeepSeek, the evaluation could complicate its push into international markets. Countries have already limited its use on government systems, and a documented control concern gives them another reason to hold that line or widen it.

The wider backdrop is the US-China contest over technology. DeepSeek's growth has tracked heightened tensions between the two countries, including disputes over export controls.

What to watch next is fairly clear. One signal is whether DeepSeek responds to the Concordia AI findings or updates V4 Pro. Another is whether Beijing's own regulators reference the evaluation. A third is whether more governments add the company to their restricted lists.

The US, Australia and the Czech Republic acted on concerns about data and censorship. The next round of decisions may hinge on a simpler question: when you tell the model to stop, does it?

data.title: Coinbase CEO Brian Armstrong Scales Back Bitcoin Prediction, Still Sees Nearly 7x Upside By 2030
data.description:
Key points:
  • Coinbase CEO Brian Armstrong said Bitcoin has likely bottomed and referred to the recent slide on the Anthropic IPO.
  • He said he still believes in Bitcoin's four-year cycles and expects a rebound.
  • With Bitcoin near $59,000, his target implied a gain of roughly 580%.

Coinbase (COIN) CEO Brian Armstrong is sticking to his long-term call that Bitcoin (BTC) could still surge nearly sevenfold by 2030, even as the token trades well below its highs.

Armstrong predicted Bitcoin could hit $400,000 “or more” by the end of the decade, speaking at the TomorrowX conference in Austin, published on Wednesday. With Bitcoin trading around $59,000, that target suggests a gain of roughly 580%.

He has held that target for some time, when he called it a reasonable goal for 2030. It sits well below the $1 million Bitcoin he predicted on Stripe's Cheeky Pint podcast in August 2025.

Bitcoin was trading for about $116,000 back then. But as of late Friday, the apex cryptocurrency was trading at $59,960, down more than 48% from its level in August 2025. Bitcoin's price is down more than 2% in the past 24 hours.

On Stocktwits, the retail sentiment around BTC moved to ‘bullish’ from ‘extremely bullish’ zone, while chatter around it shifted to ‘normal’ from ‘high’ over the past day.

Bottom Call Stays In Place

Armstrong said he believes in Bitcoin’s four-year cycles, and the timing suggests the worst was over. 'I think we've probably seen the bottom on this one,' he said. He added that the low of this cycle is still about four times the low of the last one. That leaves him optimistic about the next year or so, he said.

Armstrong attributed some of Bitcoin's latest slide to Anthropic's (ANT) IPO. He said the listing pulled money away from crypto, much as Space Exploration Technologies Corp.’s (SPCX) debut did in June. He expected Bitcoin to rebound shortly after.

Adding to his long-term outlook, he said, “Bitcoin still is a very important thing in the world of having sound money that can't be inflated, and that's going to be important in 10 years. It'll be important in 100 years.”

COIN stock edged higher after closing over 3% higher on Friday. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around COIN moved to ‘neutral’ from the ‘bullish’ zone, while chatter around it stayed at ‘normal’ levels over the past day.

data.title: India finds bacteria in second unsafe Bisleri water sample, document shows
data.description:
Indian authorities have found a sample of Bisleri-branded water to be unsafe due to coliform bacteria, a regulatory document shows, the second such finding in recent days on the nation's biggest and most popular packaged-water brand.

In an August 12 notice to Bisleri, the document shows, the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India relayed its findings to the company and asked it to prohibit the sale of the affected batch, which was manufactured in July.

The sample was tested again for confirmation and was still found unsafe, said a government official, who declined to be named as the results are not public.

Bisleri told Reuters in a statement on Saturday that it had recalled the batch in August on the government's instructions and that "the primary and referral laboratories reported the presence of coliform bacteria in the regulatory sample".

But the company said it commissioned independent testing of samples from the same batch, which found they met "the applicable standard for coliform bacteria and all other applicable food safety standards".

"The difference between the regulatory and independent findings warrants a thorough review," the company said. "Bisleri will continue to cooperate fully with FSSAI to establish the facts."

The regulator did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Reuters reported on Monday that the agency had found a sample of Bisleri water unsafe and that it would test samples from all bottled-water companies in India.

Bisleri's 20-cent bottles have made the company a household name in India, where poor water quality has turned bottled water into a necessity for homes and restaurants. It has maintained its market-leader position while competing with PepsiCo and Coca-Cola in India's packaged drinking water market, with estimates showing its valuation at more than $3.5 billion.

data.title: Ethanol policy reset: What does the shift in feedstock priorities mean for sugar mills and farmers?
data.description:
India’s ethanol blending programme has made remarkable progress, increasing blending from 1.53 per cent in 2013-14 to 20 per cent in Ethanol Supply Year (ESY) 2025-26, ahead of the original 2030 target. However, the policy flexibility that enabled sugar mills to divert sugarcane towards ethanol production has been withdrawn for 2026-27.

The Government has directed zero diversion of sugar towards ethanol production. The Oil Marketing Companies’ tender for approximately 1,100 crore litres excludes ethanol produced from sugarcane juice, sugar syrup and B-heavy molasses, leaving C-heavy molasses as the only eligible sugarcane-based feedstock.

Why the policy reset?

The decision follows concerns over tightening domestic sugar availability. The 2025-26 season ended with stocks of approximately 35 lakh tonnes, the lowest in nearly three decades. For 2026-27, gross sugar production is projected at around 310 lakh tonnes against estimated consumption of 285–290 lakh tonnes, leaving limited scope to rebuild inventories, particularly after last year’s diversion of 29 lakh tonnes.

With retail sugar inflation exceeding 30 per cent across 21 States and Union Territories in September, prioritising domestic availability is understandable. However, a complete restriction also raises concerns for an industry that has invested substantially in ethanol production capacity.

Implications for sugar mills and ethanol producers

Sugarcane juice and B-heavy molasses contributed approximately 266 crore litres of ethanol last year, supported by capacities developed under Government interest subvention schemes since 2018. Under the revised procurement framework, these capacities have no procurement route for the current supply year.

Distilleries must, therefore, shift towards C-heavy molasses, invest in grain-based production or operate below installed capacity. This also limits sugar mills’ ability to optimise their production mix.

Financial pressures add to these challenges. The minimum selling price (MSP) of sugar has remained unchanged at Rs 31 per kg since February 2019, while the Fair and Remunerative Price (FRP) of sugarcane has increased to Rs 365 per quintal for 2026-27. Meanwhile, C-heavy molasses-based ethanol procurement remains unchanged at Rs 57.97 per litre.

Although higher market sugar prices currently support mill cash flows, sustained pressure on finances could affect timely payments to farmers. A calibrated, stock-linked mechanism permitting limited B-heavy molasses diversion could balance sugar availability with existing ethanol capacity.

Growing dependence on grain-based ethanol

With sugarcane-based feedstocks largely excluded, grain-based ethanol will need to meet most procurement requirements. In 2025-26, approximately 614 crore litres were allocated to maize-based producers, of which around 413 crore litres had been delivered by September-end.

Grain distillers anticipate a 40–50 per cent increase in maize demand next year, even as the USDA projects an approximately 10 per cent decline in India’s maize output. This could intensify competition for maize, affecting prices and the poultry and animal feed industries. Surplus rice supplied by the Food Corporation of India can bridge part of the requirement, but greater grain dependence also warrants careful assessment of food security, fiscal implications and feedstock economics.

A diversified strategy guided by cost efficiency and supply reliability is therefore essential.

Towards a balanced policy framework

India’s ethanol programme now requires policy certainty alongside blending targets. Three priorities deserve attention:

First, policy predictability: Procurement decisions should be announced sufficiently in advance, allowing mills and distilleries to plan investments and operations.

Second, stock-linked diversion: Diversion limits should reflect opening stocks, production estimates and consumption, allowing flexibility when sugar supplies improve.

Third, pricing alignment: Sugar MSP, cane FRP and feedstock-specific ethanol prices must be assessed together. The committee under Prof. Ramesh Chand, reviewing sugarcane and sugar pricing, offers an opportunity to address these interdependencies, beginning with C-heavy ethanol pricing.

The objective is not to favour one feedstock over another, but to build a predictable and balanced ethanol ecosystem that safeguards sugar availability, supports farmers, protects industry investments and ensures India’s long-term energy security.

The author is Executive Director and Unit Head, Sugar, Power & Ethanol (SPE) division at Zuari Industries Limited.

data.title: Small particles, big potential: How nanotechnology is changing life on India’s farms
data.description:
For generations, feeding a field in India has meant hauling sacks: 45 kg for a bag of urea, 50 kg for DAP. Today, crop nutrition is increasingly being explored through products that fit in a farmer’s hand.

The change comes from particles too small to see. A nanometre is a billionth of a metre; a human hair is about 80,000 nanometres wide. At that scale, materials can exhibit distinct physical and chemical properties. Nutrients applied as foliar sprays may be absorbed through the leaf surface and stomatal openings, potentially improving nutrient delivery under suitable conditions. However, uptake depends on formulation, crop and environment, and smaller particle size does not automatically guarantee higher nutrient-use efficiency.

Since IFFCO launched nano urea in June 2021, India has sold nearly 16 crore bottles of nano urea and nano DAP, and approved more than a dozen new nano products this year alone. Amid disruptions in West Asia highlighting India’s reliance on imported fertilizers, nano-fertilisers have attracted interest as potential tools to improve nutrient management and reduce dependence.

Creating livelihoods

Nano is also creating livelihoods. In 2023-24, fertiliser companies handed 1,094 agricultural drones, used to spray nano fertilisers, to women’s self-help groups across 22 states, 500 of them under the Namo Drone Didi scheme. Gujarat subsidises half the cost of nano fertilisers, while Rajasthan supports spraying operations.

None of this is magic. Results vary with soil, crop and season, and nano fertilisers work best alongside the right basal dose of conventional fertiliser, as complementary tools within integrated nutrient management rather than universal substitutes for conventional fertilisers. Every product must now clear multi-location and multi-season field trials. When appropriately used, they may offer benefits under specific conditions.

IFFCO, a pioneer in India’s commercial nano-fertiliser sector, now sells nano urea, DAP, zinc and copper across the country. Nano DAP was launched at Rs 600 a bottle, against Rs 1,350 for a 50 kg bag of conventional DAP, and says its plants can make about 9.5 lakh bottles a day. However, such price comparisons should be interpreted cautiously because nutrient supply, application requirements and crop response differ between formulations.

How the outcome has to be interpreted

Coromandel International developed Gromor Nano DAP at the IIT Bombay–Monash Research Academy, and manufactures it at a Kakinada plant, with a capacity of one crore bottles a year.

Zuari FarmHub has made the process greener. Its Nano Shakti urea and DAP, developed with The Energy and Resources Institute (TERI) using beneficial bacteria, are marketed by Paradeep Phosphates as India’s first biogenic nano fertilisers. TERI says the technology has reached nearly 38 lakh acres, with yields 8 to 28 per cent higher and nitrous oxide emissions 32 to 72% lower in its field deployments. These outcomes should be interpreted in the context of the crops, locations and experimental conditions involved.

For fruit and vegetable growers, the biggest gains may come from the smallest doses. Crops need copper only in trace amounts, but a shortfall can stunt young leaves and hurt flowering and fruit set. Dr Heinisch Agro Solutions (HAS), which brings German nanotechnology to Indian farms from its base in Kangra, Himachal Pradesh, addresses this with AgroCuprum®, a nano copper fertiliser.. It has been approved in Himachal Pradesh, Haryana, Karnataka and Rajasthan, with crop-specific guidance for tomato, chilli, capsicum, cucumber and pomegranate.

Better nutrient management

The benefits reach beyond the field too. Australia’s Nanollose turns farm and food waste into microbial nanocellulose and, with India’s Birla Cellulose, has developed a tree-free fibre called Nullarbor. A pilot run in India produced 580 kg, its largest batch yet. Such innovations highlight the potential of renewable-resource-based biomaterials, although environmental benefits require life-cycle assessment.

Back on the farm, the measure is simple: better nutrient management, reduced avoidable losses, improved farm profitability and sustained crop productivity. India’s nanotechnology story is being written in particles too small to see. Its impact will be measured in what farmers can see: what is left in their pocket at season’s end.

data.title: Binance gets preliminary approval to establish Asia hub in Bhutan
data.description:
Binance said on Friday it received in-principle approval from Bhutan's Gelephu Central Bank to establish regulated digital-asset operations in the Himalayan kingdom, as part of its plans to expand into five Asian markets next year.

"The in-principle approval is a first step, not a full license and Binance must satisfy the conditions specified by GCB...before the relevant regulated activities may commence," the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange said in a statement.

Binance's expansion push follows a security breach linked to North Korea that resulted in $6.3 billion being stolen from its platform last month.

data.title: Cathie Wood-Led Ark Invest Loads Up On SPCX, CRSP And TEM — But Sells SHOP, ILMN, BYD
data.description:
Key points:
  • Ark's buying activity spanned a wider range of companies, with biotechnology names featuring prominently across Ark Innovation and Genomic Revolution ETFs.
  • Ark also purchased SpaceX shares for two consecutive days, adding over 108,000 shares of the Elon Musk-led space giant to its kitty.
  • On the selling side, Ark's activity was concentrated in three stocks, with the bulk of the reductions coming from the flagship Ark Innovation ETF.

Cathie Wood-led Ark Investment Management made several portfolio adjustments on Friday, with the firm's latest trading disclosures showing activity across its flagship Ark Innovation ETF (ARKK), Ark Genomic Revolution ETF (ARKG) and Ark Autonomous Technology & Robotics ETF (ARKQ).

Ark’s trading activity on Friday covered a mix of technology, biotechnology and electric vehicle-related stocks.

Ark Loads Up On SPCX, CRSP, TEM

Ark's buying activity spanned a wider range of companies, with biotechnology names featuring prominently across its ARKK and ARKG ETFs.

Ark purchased Space Exploration Technologies Corp. (SPCX) shares for two consecutive days, adding over 108,000 shares of the Elon Musk-led space giant to its kitty. ARKK purchased 70,601 SpaceX shares on Friday, doubling down on its purchase of 37,788 shares of the company on Wednesday.

Within ARKK, the fund added 35,772 shares of CRISPR Therapeutics AG (CRSP) and 115,086 shares of Recursion Pharmaceuticals Inc. (RXRX). It also purchased 10,114 shares of Tempus AI Inc. (TEM), adding to its exposure to the company.

The fund's other purchases included 24,873 shares of Twist Bioscience Corp. (TWST), 8,213 shares of Beam Therapeutics Inc. (BEAM) and 1,857 shares of Natera Inc. (NTRA).

Meanwhile, ARKG also added to its positions in biotechnology companies, purchasing 1,284 shares of Twist Bioscience Corp. (TWST) and 206 shares of Beam Therapeutics Inc. (BEAM). The fund additionally bought 6,538 shares of Arcturus Therapeutics Holdings Inc. (ARCT).

What Ark Sold

On the selling side, Ark's activity was concentrated in three stocks, with the bulk of the reductions coming from its flagship ARKK.

The fund sold 93,123 shares of Illumina Inc. (ILMN), representing 0.3419% of the ETF, according to the trading disclosure. It also offloaded 39,123 shares of Shopify Inc. (SHOP), equivalent to 0.1001% of ARKK.

The selling extended beyond ARKK, with the Ark Autonomous Technology & Robotics ETF (ARKQ) disposing of 296 shares of BYD Company Limited (BYDDY).

ARKK’s price closed higher by more than 3% in Friday’s regular trading session. Retail sentiment on Stocktwits around ARKK trended in the ‘bearish’ territory at the time of writing.
